name: Edward Harry Temme
highlight: First swimmer successful in both directions · 1927 and 1934
biography: Edward Harry Temme, usually known as Ted, combined Channel swimming with international water polo. Born in Plaistow in 1904, he swam for Plaistow United and worked for the Cornhill Insurance Group. His sporting life included captaining swimming and water-polo teams, representing Great Britain at the 1928 and 1936 Olympics and later managing public baths.

Temme first crossed the English Channel from France to England in August 1927. The Channel Swimming Association records 14 hours and 29 minutes. A contemporary TIME report describes his trudgeon stroke and identifies Thomas William Burgess as his coach. The Dover sources associate the crossing with the tug Alsace, although accounts differ on the exact English landing locality.

Temme completed the reverse direction in August 1934. CSA records 15 hours and 34 minutes; a contemporary Daily News report gives 15 hours and 54 minutes and dates completion to 18 August. The two successes, seven years apart, made him the first swimmer to complete the Channel in both directions; they were not a continuous return crossing. His second swim used Lady Brassey, with H. W. Pearson as pilot and Storey as trainer.

Temme remained active around the Channel after his own record swims. He coached Sam Rockett and supervised the first Daily Mail cross-Channel race in 1950. His career therefore extended from individual swimming to competition, coaching and event organisation.

lines.text: Record date 18 August is retained. The Daily News dispatch dated Monday 20 August explicitly describes the crossing as accomplished on Saturday, supporting finishDate 18 August without deriving a phase from elapsed time. Dover.UK’s 19 August remains an unresolved alternative; no overnight start/finish reconciliation is invented. The newspaper reports 15h54m, whereas CSA and the later listings publish 15h34m. Departure day and clocks remain unknown.
lines.label: Timing note

lines.text: CSA individual record 2464 publishes England–France, 1934, 15:34. Dover Museum and the CS&PF historical table give 18 August; Dover.UK gives 19 August. The original Daily News, St John’s, 21 August 1934, page 6, reports in a London dispatch dated 20 August that Temme accomplished the reverse crossing on Saturday, 18 August, in 15h54m. The explicit completion wording supports the displayed finish date, but neither the alternative date nor the duration discrepancy is reconciled. No original observer report or ratification manuscript was inspected.
Individual successful record: England, solo England–France, 1934, 15:34.
